text: In the Schwarzschild metric, the radial coordinate r is the areal radius: a sphere at coordinate value r has surface area 4πr², and it is not in general the proper distance from the center.
explanation: True. The book defines r geometrically by A = 4πr², so it is the area-radius, not a ruler distance. The proper radial distance ∫dr/√(1−r_s/r) is strictly larger than the coordinate difference r₂−r₁ because of the positive spatial curvature.
